title: Annotatio VI §.V (2a): Impious resist grace-increase — Oblation offered, Reception blocked
pass_a_gloss: (2) From the nature of Impious Eaters, because (a) they are maliciously resisting — Therefore altogether as incapable of the Increase of preventing divine grace (which increase is to be placed in Christ’s spiritually vivifying body), so unworthy of the same. You except, distinguishing Reception and Retention of Christ’s flesh — the former to be granted to the Impious, not the latter. Reply: It is more rightly distinguished here (as Lutherans elsewhere are wont) between Oblation and Reception — of which the former indeed applies to the Impious through Christ’s Grace; the latter not likewise, because of their obstinate malice, which itself, since it alone impedes Retention of Christ’s flesh, also by like reason impedes Reception of the same; otherwise there would be no cause why, the Communicant’s malice obstructing, Christ’s flesh could nevertheless not be retained equally as, the same malice obstructing, it could be received and eaten.
pass_b_english: (2a) From Impious eaters’ nature: they maliciously resist, so they are incapable of — and unworthy of — the increase of preventing grace placed in Christ’s vivifying body.

Do not split Reception vs Retention to give Impious reception. Better (as Lutherans elsewhere): Oblation reaches them by grace; Reception does not — the same obstinate malice that blocks retention blocks reception.
source_text: (2) Ex natura Manducantium Impiorum, quia (a) sunt malitiosè repugnantes, Ergo Augmenti gratiæ divinæ prævenientis (quale augmentum in corpore Christi spiritualiter vivificante reponendum est) omnino ut incapaces, ita eodem indigni. Excipis, distinguendo inter Receptionem, & Retentionem carnis Christi; prius concedendum esse Impiis, non verò posterius. Respond. Rectius distingui hîc (ut aliàs Lutherani solent) inter Oblationem & Receptionem, quarum prior quidem competit in Impios per Gratiam Christi; posterior non item, ob malitiam eorum obstinatam, quæ ipsa quia Retentionem carnis Christi impedit sola, etiam pari ratione Receptionem ejusdem; Alias causa nulla esset, quare, obstante licèt Communicantis malitia, retineri tamen caro Christi non posset æquè, atque, obstante licet ejusdem malitia, recipi atque manducari.
